newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa truckers to step up strike action - union.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa truckers to step up strike action - union.

text.p: A national truckers strike by between 30,000 to 40,000 workers across South Africa was expected to accelerate on Thursday following a breakdown in mediation on Wednesday night, a union official said.

"We came close to settling around midnight but in the end employers were not ready to make an improved offer," Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU) national organiser Thulani Dlamini told Reuters.
He expected workers to intensify their strike action -- which started Wednesday -- and has so far taken the form of pickets at companies which have resorted to employing scab labour in the industry.
Employers and the seven unions organised in the sector are deadlocked over wages and working conditions.
Dlamini said the union had been given a mandate from workers to press for a 14 percent across-the-board increase.
Employers' response at Wednesday night's mediation meeting had been that the unions "be more creative in putting together a 14 percent package," he said.
South Africa's giant trade union federation Cosatu said on Thursday it supported the strikers and said the refusal of employers to meet the unions' demands across the board was irresponsible.

"The speculations on what this strike will do to the value of the rand and its decline should be placed firmly on the shoulders of the employers," the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) said in a statement.

Road Freight Employers' Association chairman Johan van der Walt said in a statement on Thursday the unions had been inflexibile in moving from their mandated position of 14 to 18 percent, previously between 12.5 and 18 percent.

"The association remains flexible to explore possible areas of settlement beyond its final position which constitutes a wage increase between 10 to 15 percent and is prepared to continue with the mediation proces," van der Walt said.
Dlamini said the unions were now waiting to hear from the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration whether employers would come forward with an improved offer.
"The situation is uncertain if and when employers are ready to make an improved offer," he said.
Intensified pickets were planned throughout the country at selected companies that employed scab labour, he added.
The trucking strike is the first in the sector in fifty years and also the first nationwide strike under the New Labour Relations Act.
It has the potential to disrupt major sectors of the economy, including banking, air freight, waste companies, livestock vehicles, and the ferrying of chemicals and fuels.
